name: Smoked snoek pâté
summary: Flaked smoked snoek beaten with cream cheese, lemon and parsley into a smoky, lemony spread for lunch or a party table.
about: Snoek is the Cape's signature fish, sold smoked at West Coast farm stalls and fish shops. Turning a piece of smoked snoek, or the braai leftovers, into a pâté is a long-standing Cape lunch and party habit, and the pâté is spread thickly and eaten with lemon.

ingredients.name: Smoked snoek
ingredients.note: about 250 g once skinned and boned

ingredients.name: Lemon
ingredients.note: zest and juice of half, rest in wedges

steps: Skin the snoek and flake it into a bowl, running your fingers through the flakes to find and remove every bone. This takes about 10 minutes and is worth doing slowly.
In another bowl, beat the cream cheese and sour cream with a wooden spoon for 1 minute, until smooth and soft.
Fold in the snoek, lemon zest, spring onions, parsley and paprika, mashing lightly with a fork. Stop when it is spreadable but still has some texture.
Add the lemon juice a little at a time, tasting as you go, and season with pepper. Smoked snoek is salty, so add salt only if it needs it.
Spoon into a bowl and chill for at least 15 minutes, until firm enough to hold its shape. Serve with crackers or toast and lemon wedges.
prepNote: Keeps 3 days covered in the fridge and freezes well for a month.
